Definition: from G5204; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply:--water-pot.
BiblicalUsage: hydría means a water-jar, a water-pot. In John 2:6, the text says "And there were set there six waterpots of stone." In John 4:28, the text says "The woman then left her waterpot."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading hydría this way, I believe God provides, and His provision is enough — even when it does not look like we expected. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Turns Water into Wine at Cana; Jesus and the Samaritan Woman
